Book signal review ┬À first-pass mechanical backtest

215 batches. 58 crypto futures. One fee-inclusive test bed.

Every strategy section was mapped to a mechanical proxy, signalled on its own timeframe, and executed on 1-minute Binance USDT-M data with taker fees, slippage and historical funding. Signals use completed bars only; entries occur at the first 1m open after the signal bar closes.

01 ┬À Horizon

Fees break the fast timeframes

The average 5m trade is -0.043% gross before costs and -0.143% net after. The cost stack adds about 0.100% per round trip ÔÇö enough to turn a flat gross edge into a clear loss.

5m: 41 specs ┬À 16,523,515 trades ┬À only 1% of symbol-spec pairs positive
02 ┬À Edge

Daily edge is thin and uneven

Daily specs average 0.72% net per trade, but the median symbol earns 0.018%; 68% of specs are positive, only 49% of symbol-spec pairs. The average is carried by a minority of strong symbols.

Median daily portfolio 4.5% over 4 years ┬À BTC 238% ┬À fee drag 0.13%/trade
03 ┬À Benchmark

Buy & hold is a high bar

BTC returned 238% and the equal-weight crypto basket 208% from Aug 2022 to Aug 2026. Most mechanical proxies do not beat it after costs.

Daily flow is 64% long; in a +238% BTC market, directional beta is part of the result.
04 ┬À Coverage

145 of 215 batches survived the first screen

274 high/medium-confidence proxies (159 unique rules) were tested. 23 batches only contain low-confidence mappings, 14 are excluded, and 33 have no strategy sections.

Top result: G1 (1d, double_pattern) ┬À 3.75% median symbol net, 61% of symbols positive

Coverage map

How the 215 batch folders were classified. The dashboard never silently drops a batch.

Coverage is intentionally conservative. A section is only ÔÇ£testedÔÇØ if a mechanical rule could be mapped with high or medium confidence. Complex discretionary patterns, non-crypto assets and pure exit/position variants are listed with reasons instead of being silently approximated.

Data & execution

OHLCV data comes from D:\1mDataBinance. Higher timeframes are built from monthly Binance CSVs (5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d); weekly bars are resampled from daily. Execution uses 1-minute OHLC, including mixed CSV/parquet months.

  • Signal timing: only completed strategy-TF bars. Entry at the first 1m open after the signal bar closes.
  • Stops / targets: checked on 1m OHLC. If stop and target touch in the same 1m bar, the stop is assumed first (conservative).
  • Exit time / signal: next 1m open after the exit bar closes.
  • One position per symbol per strategy. No pyramiding, no overlapping entries.
  • Funding: historical 8h funding from 151_M\binance_futures\funding, charged to the position side.

Cost model

Binance USDT-M taker fee 0.0005 per side and slippage 0.0002 per side. A round trip costs roughly 14 bps before funding. The dashboard reports both gross and net so the cost drag is visible.

Portfolio math

Each trade is sized at 1/58 of capital. Monthly PnL is summed across symbols and compounded. This is a conservative equal-weight deployment: idle symbols leave cash uninvested. Benchmarks are fully invested and are shown for context, not as a like-for-like comparison.

Mapping confidence

  • High: the section names an explicit indicator/pattern family and parameters could be parsed (e.g. MACD cross, RSI level, Donchian channel, Bollinger band).
  • Medium: the family is clear but the source leaves thresholds or filters implicit; a standard parameter set is used.
  • Low: only a loose keyword match; not included in the main results. These sections are listed as ÔÇ£low confidence onlyÔÇØ at batch level.
  • Excluded: options, US equities, FX, Nifty, news/macro, portfolio/rotation, pure exit or position-sizing variants, and discretionary patterns (SMC, Elliott, harmonic, Wyckoff, TD sequential, divergence).
  • Duplicate rules: 274 source mappings collapse to 166 unique engine rules. The explorer marks duplicates with ├ùN and defaults to unique rules.

Known limitations

  • This is a first-pass mechanical proxy, not a claim of exact replication of every discretionary rule in the source book.
  • Weekly strategies are tested on weekly bars resampled from daily; intraweek path is approximated by 1m execution after the weekly close.
  • Cross-sectional, breadth, pairs and portfolio-rotation rules are out of scope for a single-symbol engine.
  • Symbol coverage is survivorship-biased: the 58 symbols are those with higher-timeframe CSVs in the local archive. The equal-weight basket also enters new listings at their first available month.
  • Funding is applied at 8h boundaries; small timing differences versus exchange settlement are possible.
  • New listings can produce extreme single-trade returns. The dashboard therefore ranks on median symbol net and reports symbol consistency; average net and portfolio return are shown but should be read with that caveat.
  • All fills are taker fills. Maker execution, fee rebates or lower slippage would materially improve the fast timeframes; the fee stack is the dominant result for 5m/15m/1h.
Result files: strategy_metrics.csv, dashboard_data.json, and per-symbol parquet summaries under results\summary and results\monthly.
